summary: Zhejiang University admits non-Chinese citizens to doctoral programmes of 3 to 4 years, taught in Chinese or English, through its International College. Applicants need a master's degree, are generally under 40, and apply online with a personal statement of about 1,500 words and two recommendation letters. Funding routes include the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type A and Type B), the Zhejiang Government Scholarship, a China Studies fellowship, school-level scholarships and self-funded places. The application fee is RMB 800.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens holding an ordinary passport for private purposes. Former Chinese citizens or people who acquired foreign citizenship at birth must submit nationality status documents.

Applicants need a master's degree and should be under 40; the age limit may be relaxed for healthy applicants with substantial relevant work experience and strong academic ability. Graduating students can use a pre-graduation or student status certificate and must give the original degree certificate by registration. Applicants must have good moral conduct, good health, academic excellence and no record of legal violations.

Language: Chinese-taught programmes need a valid HSK Level 5 certificate with 180 points or more (some programmes ask for more, see the catalogue). English-taught programmes need IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 90 (centre-based or Home Edition), Duolingo 120, Cambridge C1 Advanced 180 or Cambridge C2 Proficiency 180. Exemptions: a bachelor's or master's degree taught in Chinese or English at an accredited institution (with a certificate of instruction), Chinese-medium secondary schooling (for Chinese-taught programmes), or English as native language (listed countries include the UK, US, Canada, Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, South Africa, Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Singapore and others). Some programmes give priority to applicants with an English test result.

Many programmes require, or suggest, a Form for Provisional Acceptance by a ZJU supervisor, and applicants are told to contact supervisors before applying; applicants who cannot obtain one may still apply to programmes where it is not marked as required. Some routes have extra eligibility, for example the Zhejiang Government Scholarship and CSC Type B need the applicant to be under 40 for doctoral study and not to hold another scholarship at the same time, and the College of Optical Science and Engineering scholarship needs a degree from a QS top-50 university (or, for Belt and Road countries, one of the top three universities of the home country in those rankings).
age_experience_notes: Under age 40; the limit may be relaxed for healthy applicants with substantial relevant work experience and strong academic ability. No minimum work experience is stated.
funding_summary: Funding depends on the route. CSC Type B covers tuition waiver, free on-campus accommodation or an accommodation allowance, a stipend under the relevant standard and comprehensive medical insurance (amounts not given on the ZJU pages). The Zhejiang Government Scholarship gives 30,000 yuan for one year (students with excellent performance may reapply). The College of Optical Science and Engineering scholarship covers tuition, on-campus accommodation, comprehensive medical insurance and a stipend of RMB 3,500 per month. The ZJE Hai scholarship (2026 notice) covers tuition waiver, free on-campus accommodation and up to RMB 3,000 per month for 10 months a year for four years. Self-funded students pay tuition of RMB 37,800 to 47,800 per year in the English-taught catalogue. CSC Type A coverage is set by the dispatching authority and is not described on the ZJU notice.
programmes_note: Doctoral programmes last 3 to 4 academic years. The English-taught catalogue (2027) lists about 83 entries across the humanities, social sciences, sciences, engineering, information, agriculture, life science and environment faculties and the ZJU-Edinburgh Institute (International Campus); the Chinese-taught catalogue is a separate PDF. Many entries say a supervisor acceptance form is required, suggested, or gives priority. Catalogues may change, so check the website. Scholarship fields: China Studies fellowship for humanities and social science doctoral programmes (including Psychology); ZJE Hai for ZJE doctoral programmes; Optical scholarship for College of Optical Science and Engineering programmes; China-ASEAN Oceanic Scholarship for Ocean College programmes.
institutions_note: Single host university: Zhejiang University, with faculties of Humanities, Social Science, Science, Engineering, Information, Agriculture, Life Science and Environment, plus the Zhejiang University-University of Edinburgh Institute at the International Campus (dual-degree option) and the International School of Medicine. Applicants choose a programme in the online system; the catalogue shows which school runs each programme and links to the school's website.

summary.detail: Doctoral programmes of 3 to 4 academic years, taught in Chinese (the larger catalogue) or English. Applicants need a master's degree; the application deadline for most programmes is 28 February 2027 (Beijing time) and 31 May 2027 for specially marked programmes. Tuition in the English-taught catalogue is RMB 37,800 (humanities), RMB 42,800 (most programmes), RMB 45,000 (Chinese Law) and RMB 47,800 (ZJE) per year. Newly admitted students are expected to enrol in early September 2027.

benefits.conditions: Depends on the route granted. Self-funded students pay RMB 37,800 to 47,800 per year (English-taught catalogue); the Zhejiang Government Scholarship is a fixed 30,000 yuan.

benefits.limit_text: CSC Type B stipend 'under the relevant standard' (no amount stated); Optical scholarship RMB 3,500 per month; ZJE Hai up to RMB 3,000 per month for 10 months a year (2026 notice); Zhejiang Government Scholarship 30,000 yuan for one year
benefits.conditions: ZJE Hai stipend: full month if registered on or before the 15th, half a month if later; stops on leave, dropping out, long absence or returning home after graduation (from the 2026 notice).

benefits.limit_text: Free on-campus accommodation or an accommodation allowance under CSC Type B; on-campus accommodation under the Optical scholarship; free on-campus accommodation under ZJE Hai (2026 notice)
benefits.conditions: The university generally assigns graduate housing and tells students the address at registration. Not included in the Zhejiang Government Scholarship amount stated.

benefits.limit_text: Comprehensive medical insurance under CSC Type B and the Optical scholarship; the university's scheme is RMB 800 for a 12-month period
benefits.conditions: The insurance page covers accidental injury, outpatient, inpatient care and death or disability, limited to public hospitals in mainland China, and excludes dental work, glasses, delivery and conditions diagnosed before arrival. It does not say whether scholarship holders must buy it separately.
Applications without the fee paid by the deadline are invalid. CSC Type A applicants do not pay the application fee.

benefits.limit_text: No travel support is mentioned on the ZJU notices read

requirements.text: Passport information page; the passport must be valid on or after 1 March 2028.

Original master's degree certificate. Graduating students give a pre-graduation or student status certificate and must provide the original by registration. Degrees from outside mainland China may need an Academic Credential Evaluation Report from CSCSE at registration.
Complete transcripts for bachelor's and master's studies.
Language proficiency certificate as set in the ZJU language requirements (or an exemption document such as a certificate of instruction), uploaded in the Language Proficiency Certificate section.
Personal statement of about 1,500 words in Chinese or English covering academic background, work experience, reasons for applying and a research proposal.
Two recommendation letters, generally from full or associate professors in the field, showing the signer's signature, phone number and email.

application_steps.title: Pick a programme and contact a supervisor
application_steps.detail: Choose a doctoral programme in the 2027 English-taught or Chinese-taught catalogue and check its language, tuition and supervisor-form rule. Contact supervisors before applying (email with CV and personal statement is recommended) to get the Form for Provisional Acceptance; you can still apply if you cannot get one, unless the catalogue says it is required.

application_steps.title: Apply online and upload all documents
application_steps.detail: Register in the online application system, choose Program Type, Doctoral Degree and your major, upload everything at submission (supplementary materials are generally not accepted, and nothing is posted or emailed), and submit. Pay the RMB 800 fee online by the deadline or by remittance with the remittance letter uploaded. Most programmes close on 28 February 2027 (Beijing time); marked programmes close on 31 May 2027; CSC Type B closes on 31 December 2026.

application_steps.title: Choose scholarships in the same submission
application_steps.detail: You may apply for several scholarships but submit once, by the earliest applicable deadline, ticking every scholarship you want; later additions are not allowed. CSC Type A is applied for through your home country's dispatching authority (ZJU does not take Type A applications directly), and Type B is applied for in the CSC system with agency number 10335 and in the ZJU system.

application_steps.title: Document review and video interview
application_steps.detail: The university reviews materials and qualified applicants are interviewed by video, arranged by the academic school. Admission is competitive and considers research ability, academic performance, language proficiency and interview performance.

application_steps.title: Scholarship nomination and results
application_steps.detail: For CSC Type B, pre-admission notices go to qualified applicants between March and April, the nomination list goes to CSC for review, and awardees are announced on the ZJU International Admissions website in late July or early August 2027. For the Zhejiang Government Scholarship results are posted in the application system, and for the Optical scholarship results are sent by email. Final admission results are usually released in late July or early August.

application_steps.title: Download the Admission Notice and arrange the visa
application_steps.detail: Download the Admission Notice from the system; the e-Confirmation Form for Study in China (used for the visa) is sent to your email. Hard copies are no longer provided. Self-funded students who receive a pre-admission notice must pay first-year tuition through the system within the stated deadline or the pre-admission is cancelled.

application_steps.title: Register in early September 2027 and keep the award conditions
application_steps.detail: Newly admitted students are expected to enrol in early September 2027. CSC Type B recipients follow CSC Chinese Government Scholarship regulations and may not change institution, programme or study duration in the Admission Notice. Students who cannot register, suspend or withdraw for health or personal reasons lose Zhejiang Government Scholarship eligibility.
